headline: Steroids kill neurons
body: and this is the exact mechanism

headline: The experiment
body: Cortical neurons grown from rat brain tissue. | Dosed with different androgens for 24 hours or 3 days. | Three separate death readouts measured.
punch: Mitochondrial activity, LDH release, and caspase 3/7.

headline: What those measure
body: *Mitochondrial activity* tells you if the cell can still make energy. | *LDH release* means the membrane is breaking down and contents are leaking out. | *Caspase 3/7* is the enzyme that executes *apoptosis*, which is programmed cell death.
punch: Three different angles on the same question.

headline: Testosterone
body: nandrolone and trenbolone all killed neurons by apoptosis. | All three raised LDH release, so membranes were failing. | Caspase 3/7 went up, so the death was programmed, not accidental.
punch: The cells were told to die. They did not just break.

headline: Stanozolol
body: killed them a different way. | It caused *necrosis* instead of apoptosis, and did not raise LDH the same way. | Necrosis is uncontrolled rupture, which triggers inflammation in surrounding tissue.
punch: Not safer. A messier death with an inflammatory tail.

headline: Trenbolone
body: reduced *neurite outgrowth*. Neurites are the extensions neurons use to connect to each other. | It also downregulated *Tubb3*, the gene for beta 3 tubulin. | That is the structural protein neurons build those extensions from.
punch: It kills cells and stops the survivors wiring up.

headline: Nandrolone
body: hit mitochondria first. | Reduced mitochondrial activity by **24 hours**, before the apoptosis signal. | It gets in earlier in the death pathway than the others.
punch: Deca reaches the failure point sooner.

headline: Now the mechanism
body: They added *flutamide*, which blocks the androgen receptor. | The toxicity almost completely disappeared. | Mitochondria kept working. Membranes held. Apoptosis was inhibited.
punch: Block the receptor and the neurons live.

headline: Which is the problem
body: The receptor killing the neurons is the **same receptor** producing the anabolic effect. | There is no version where you block one and keep the other. | This is on target damage, not a contaminant.
punch: You cannot supplement around your own mechanism.

headline: So what actually helps
body: Antioxidants have not been tested against this. There is no evidence they help here. | Diet has not been tested against this either. | The only intervention shown to prevent it blocks the receptor you are using.
punch: Nobody has shown a way to mitigate this.

headline: What does change it
body: Toxicity was **dose dependent** in these studies. | Repeated exposure was worse than single dose. | Compound choice mattered. Trenbolone hit gene expression and neurite outgrowth when others did not.
punch: Dose. Duration. Compound. There is no fourth lever.

headline: The limits
body: This is cell culture. Concentrations in a dish are not doses in a person. | But nobody has run the study showing adolescent use is neurologically safe either. | Only one side of that uncertainty ever gets mentioned.
punch: Unstudied is not the same as cleared.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms. Real citations. No protocols.
